title: Crepes

items.raw: 3 tablespoons (42 g) unsalted butter, melted, plus more for the pan
1 tablespoon sugar (leave out for savory crepes)
Sweet: butter and sugar with lemon; Nutella and banana; jam; berries and whipped cream
Savory: ham and Gruyère; sautéed mushrooms and spinach; a fried egg

steps.text: Put the flour, eggs, milk, water, melted butter, sugar, and salt in a blender and blend 10 seconds until smooth. Or whisk the eggs and milk into the flour a little at a time to avoid lumps.

Cover and let stand at least 30 minutes at room temperature, or refrigerate up to 2 days. Resting relaxes the flour so the crepes are tender, not rubbery. It should be the consistency of heavy cream; thin with a splash of milk if needed.
Heat an 8- to 10-inch nonstick or well-seasoned crepe pan over medium heat. Brush lightly with butter.
Lift the pan off the heat, pour in about 3 tablespoons of batter, and immediately tilt and swirl so it coats the bottom in a thin, even layer.
Cook 1 to 1½ minutes, until the edges look dry and lacy and the underside is golden in spots. Loosen the edge with a spatula and flip. Cook 20 to 30 seconds more.
Slide onto a plate and repeat, buttering the pan every few crepes. Stack them as they are done; they will not stick together.
Fill each crepe and fold into quarters or roll up. For hot fillings, add them to the crepe in the pan after flipping and fold it there.

notes.label: The first one is always bad
notes.text: it seasons the pan and tells you whether the heat and batter are right. Eat it yourself.

notes.label: Ahead of time
notes.text: cooked crepes keep 3 days refrigerated or 2 months frozen, stacked between parchment and well wrapped. Rewarm in a dry pan.

notes.label: Too thick
notes.text: if the crepes come out thick or won’t spread, thin the batter with a tablespoon of milk at a time.

notes.label: Crêpes Suzette
notes.text: warm butter, sugar, orange juice, and zest in a skillet, fold the crepes into it, and serve warm.

openQuestion: This is a best guess — basic crepes with sweet and savory fillings. Who makes these, and when — a birthday breakfast, Sunday mornings, dessert? Which filling is the family favorite?
